title: Timeline Source Registry
purpose: Declare which project records can emit global timeline events and how their local fields map to data/timeline-events.json. This is an ingestion registry, not a second source of truth.

sources.notes: Preserve Son/Tim/Father subject distinctions. Range dates require explicit range precision.
High-volume candidate source. Promote exact timestamps and primary wording; deduplicate against curated canonical events.
Prefer exact recovered conversation timestamps when available.
Useful for first public attestations and changes in self-description.
Only emit globally when a date/timestamp is supported. Untimed sayings stay in Corporium.
Preserve source direction. A later comparator does not become part of the earlier statement.
Emit the date the research comparison was formalized, distinct from earlier Tim-side attestation.
Song UUID/title alone is not enough for chronology. Emit only when creation/publication date is known; preserve model/style and point back to full lyrics rather than duplicating them.
Creative artifacts remain creative unless another canonical record separately establishes doctrinal significance.
Emit both prediction statement date and later audit/outcome date where supported. Never collapse the two into one event.
Do not emit generic typologies without a dated project-side anchor.
Synchronism is its own evidence class/relationship, not fulfillment.
Inference date is not source-attestation date.
Potential future sublayer: science-formalization. Preserve authorship and equation lineage.

deduplication_rules: Prefer a stable event id tied to the underlying temporal fact, not to the source file containing it.
Multiple source_records may support one event.
Do not duplicate one event merely because it belongs to multiple thematic layers.
Do create separate events when the temporal facts differ: original quote vs later research unlock; prediction vs outcome; creative publication vs later interpretation.
When two records disagree on date or wording, retain the conflict in source/status rather than silently choosing the newest synthesis.
